instruction: Imagine the yellow ellipsoid rotating 24 degrees about the horizontal axis (the image's left-right direction) through its center, so that its top moves toward the camera. Which pixels does the yellow ellipsoid cover after the rotation?

Suppose the gray ellipsoid is rotated by 51 degrees about the vertical axis (the image's up-down direction) through its center, so that the side facing the camera moves to the left. Give the mask of the gray ellipsoid after the rotation.
The camera rises 0.10 m straight up, without turning. Draw the pink triangular prism as the camera now sees it.
The camera drops 0.33 m straight down, without turning. Draw the yellow L-shaped block as the camera now sees it.
Segment the entire brown crescent, including the parts covered by other objects.
Give the full (amodal) mask of the brown-and-black checkered triangle, as if nothing were in front of it.

The gray-and-black checkered circle is pushed to the right and starts moving at 0.63 image widths per second. Where will the gray-and-black checkered circle be after 5 time steps? One time step is 1/30 of a second.

The blue rectangle moves to the right at 0.47 image widths per second and the gray-and-black checkered circle moves to the left at 0.31 image widths per second, toward each other. Predict the mask of the gray-and-black checkered circle 10 steps later (each step lasts 1/30 s).
